main_text.l: XXXII. Oecumenius, posteriori quidem, sed nec adeo certæ ætatis; Commentario in Epist. ad Hebræos, passim eam Paulo adscribit. Imprimis in triplici ὑποθέσει[?] seu argumento Epistolæ in limine præfixo. Quorum primum depromptum ex Athanasio in synopsi, alterum inscriptum Theodoreto, de quo suprà; tertium pluribus & urgentissimis rationibus evinci esse Paulinam. Et quidem primò, respondet objectionibus quæ petuntur à diversitate styli, aut à nomine non præfixo: secundò [illegible, ~6 letters] Pauli esse Epistolam probat μαρτυρεῖται δὲ καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐξῆς ἡ Ἐπιστολὴ ὑπάρχουσα Παύλου. 1. τῷ γεγράφθαι, ὅτι ἡ τῆς δεσμοῖς μου συνεπαθήσατε[?], 2. καὶ ἐν τῷ λέγειν, περισσότερον εὔχεσθε, ἵνα τάχιον ἀποκατασταθῶ ὑμῖν; 3. καὶ ἐν τῷ λέγειν, γινώσκετε τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἡμῶν Τιμόθεον ἀπολελυμένον &c. Ubi triplici argumento ex ipsâ Epistolâ mutuato probari dicit, quod sit Pauli, 1. dum scribit, Nam & de vinculis meis condoluistis; dum dicit, Orate am-plius;

page.notes: The Greek is small and heavily worn. The Greek words are my best reading. The word after "secundò" and the Greek word after "ὑποθέσει" are not legible enough to confirm. The line "ὅτι ἡ τῆς δεσμοῖς μου συνεπαθήσατε" is a reconstruction from the visible letters and is marked [?]. The running head reads "Autbore" in the scan; I have read it as "Authore" and marked it [?]. The final line "plius;" sits at the right margin as the second half of "am-plius;".
